title: All 8 extension-server AGENTS.md Restrictions sections summarize the workspace git-push policy as 'push freely, no pull --rebase ritual' but drop the workspace AGENTS.md's stop-and-ask-on-rejection clause — looser policy than the workspace mandates
description:
**Divergence** — per-crate AGENTS.md git-push policy summary:
- All 8 extension-server AGENTS.md Restrictions sections (e.g. crate-jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md L140, crate-jmap-chat-server/AGENTS.md L170, etc.) read: 'Push freely — `git push`, no `pull --rebase` ritual'

**Workspace AGENTS.md** "Git Commit and Push Policy" section reads: 'Push freely too: just `git push`. ... If a push is rejected for any reason — non-fast-forward, network, auth, anything — **stop and ask the human**. Do NOT run `git pull --rebase`...'

**Drift**: the per-crate summary preserves only the first half of the policy ("push freely, no pull --rebase ritual") and not the stop-and-ask-on-rejection safety clause. A contributor reading the per-crate AGENTS.md in isolation might infer "if push is rejected, just pull --rebase like every other repo" — which the workspace AGENTS.md explicitly forbids.

**Maintainer / safety cost**: this is a real safety policy ("non-fast-forward push has destroyed work in this repo before" per the workspace AGENTS.md). The summarisation drops the safety-relevant clause from the place a contributor is most likely to read first (per-crate AGENTS.md when working in that crate).

**Fix**: rewrite the 8 sibling AGENTS.md Restrictions push-policy lines to preserve the stop-and-ask-on-rejection clause, or replace the inline summary with a pointer "see workspace AGENTS.md 'Git Commit and Push Policy' for full rules". Pure doc sweep.
